page.layout: One column: ornament band, then centred title in capitals and roman, then one stanza-block of verse in italic. No margin text. Page number at head. Closing word FINIS centred below the verse.

l.i: QUEM nō mille manus, nō mille pericula mortis
Quem nec & insidiis sternere quivit Iber,
Quem nequit Mars ipse ferox, fera sica peremit,
Sica HENRICORUM sanguinolenta nece.
Scilicet occubuit scelerata fraude petitus
Arte, dolo, insidiis Rex, IUDAITA, tuis.
Quid sceleris[?] latuit tanti sub corde Monarchæ,
Vt scelerate tuo vulnere concideret?
Sedibus eximiis te, & rursum in honore locauit,
Diuitiisque auxit, muneraque ampla dedit.
Et plus quam par est, & ipse maiora tulisti,
Gratia pro meritis hæc referenda fuit?
Vt cumulo adviceret[?], proprio te CORDE beavit,
Quid maius proprio quis dare CORDE potest?
Nunc cape COR toties à te mucrone fetum[?],
HARLÆVS votis annuit ipse tuis.
Sed pariter cum DENTE, COR vt referatur eodē,
Non sunt, diversis contumulanda locis
Quæ Natura simul iunxit, quæ Parca revulsit,
Usa instrumentis pestis amara tuis.

page.notes: Head: running head absent; no catchword or signature printed. Small star-shaped mark in the text block at the line "nece." (right side, about level with the line) is a printer's or reader's mark with no printed note text; not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "sceleris" (accent over i uncertain), "adviceret" (the word between "Vt cumulo" and "te" may be adducere/adduceret or similar), "fetum" (initial letter uncertain, possibly f or long s with crossbar). "IUDAITA" is capitalised as printed; u/v normalised per rule. "tantisub" and "Quidmaius" are run-together printed words, given as separated. "Quiuit" normalised to "quivit", "beauit" to "beavit", "reuulsit" to "revulsit".
